## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6e79f90356582f6d4e1dcc57a8c64319238f9532`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.test.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/ChatbotEnhanced.answerSource-31868.test.tsx, content/docs/references/ai/object-query-source.mdx

Read to judge, not reviewed (outside the diff, on `main` at merge base `c37e47a5b`): `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/AnswerSource.tsx`, `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/mapMessages.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-read-filter.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts`. Card #33824: body and all 9 comments read. The route this PR implements is seat route A (6918602381), which says of itself that it is not a maintainer ruling; the only maintainer ruling on the card is the p1 grade (6918081689).

`Security-touching: yes` because the changed `.describe()` and header teach how row-restriction scope is reported to the person who asked.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: `scope` moves from `z.literal('visible_to_you')` to `z.enum(['visible_to_you', 'all_records'])`. One new accepted VALUE on an existing key; no new key, no default, still required. Every block that parsed before parses the same; a missing `scope` and any third value are still refused. Right, and a pure widening.
- Type surface: `ObjectQuerySource['scope']` widens from the literal to the two-value union. A TypeScript reader that assigned it to the literal type no longer compiles; the two in-repo readers (`AnswerSource.tsx`, `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`) only compare it. Right; the changeset's "a reader that switches on `scope` handles the new value" covers it.
- Export list: unchanged (`ObjectQuerySourceSchema`, `ObjectQuerySource`, `OBJECT_QUERY_SOURCE_TOOL_NAMES`). `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json` and `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` are byte-unchanged in the diff, which is right: both list names and keys, and `ai/ObjectQuerySource:scope` was already listed.
- Reader behaviour: before this head, `detectAnswerSource` (`mapMessages.ts`, `ObjectQuerySourceSchema.safeParse`) refused an `all_records` block and the turn drew no "How this was computed" block. From this head it lifts, and `AnswerSourceSection` draws the access line only for `visible_to_you`. The new test group pins that, in the `en` fallback and the zh pack. Right.
- Producers in this repo: none. `resultSourceBlock` has no definition under `packages/`; the only other parser of the block is the console's. No MCP tool and no client SDK method reads or writes `scope` (`git grep` of the head for `visible_to_you`, `all_records` as a scope value, `ObjectQuerySource`: spec, the console chat, tests and changelogs only).
- Generated reference page: the one changed row repeats the `.describe()` text word for word. Right as generated output; its truth is judged in ④.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/33824-ask-source-scope-all-records.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor. AGENTS.md (Workflow rule 3): a new accepted value is `Metadata-protocol: added`, and a kind takes at least minor on a package the diff moves. Minor is right. No other released package's source moves (the console change is a test file), so no second package entry is owed.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial on the PR body and on the changeset body, with the same arm. Right: nothing that parsed is refused.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is line-initial on both. Right by the rule's own words (accepted value), and it is what makes minor mandatory rather than patch.
- No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker: none owed for a widening with nothing to migrate.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, `open_questions` of report 6918536912 (A / B / C): answered by seat route 6918602381 with A. That answer is a seat route, not the maintainer's word. It stays escalated to the Tier H approval, and S1 below is a fact that approval needs.
- Dev flag, "the console reader needs no edit": confirmed in `AnswerSource.tsx` (`SCOPE_VISIBLE_TO_YOU` comparison) and `mapMessages.ts`.
- Dev flag, `Skills-docs: none`: `git grep` of the head finds no skill naming the block or its scope. Confirmed.
- Docs-drift comment 6933788246: `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx` names `ObjectQuerySourceSchema` in two changelog lines. Neither states the value set; nothing there is made false. Release-owned, untouched, correct.
- Version skew, for #34411 (not a finding on this PR): a console built before this spec version refuses an `all_records` block whole, so that turn shows no "How this was computed" block and no access line. That degrades to silence, never to a false statement, but the cloud producer should start answering `all_records` only once the served console carries this version.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join in this diff. Nothing to flag.
- Check-runs on the head: 65 runs at the last of four reads over about twelve minutes. 32 success, 9 skipped (opt-in and queue-only jobs), 0 failed, 0 cancelled, 24 still in progress: Test Core shards 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of 8, Test UI shards 1 to 16 of 16, Type Check UI and Type Check · workspace. Green so far includes Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Lint & Repo Gates with every Lint sub-job, Type Check source gates, consumer gates and debt ledger, and Test Core 4 of 8. No red to sign. ⛔ The gate verdict is NOT complete on this head: the two suites that run this diff's own tests (Test Core for the spec file, Test UI for the console harness) had not answered. This record's PASS is the contract judgment; the seat re-reads the check-runs before it adopts the record and before any queue step.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts` against the card's acceptance 2 and seat route A.

What holds. The direction that would be a security-class misstatement is `all_records` stated while a restriction applied. Read against `getReadFilter` on `main`, the rule the contract names does not produce it: `undefined` is answered only for a system context or when every composed layer (organization wall, row-level policies, controlled-by-parent, delegated business-unit scope, sharing) contributes nothing; a principal-less context, a caller resolving no permission set, an on-behalf-of context that cannot be intersected and every resolution failure answer the deny filter, never `undefined`. A two-value required field with no default keeps the statement mandatory, and the reader says nothing for `all_records` rather than asserting completeness. The choice of A over an optional key is sound.

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts`, the `scope` description and the header sentence (and the changeset and PR body that repeat them): the rule "`all_records` when `getReadFilter` answered `undefined`" does not deliver the card's acceptance 2 for an organization owner on every tenancy posture, and the contract does not say so. `getReadFilter` composes the organization wall as its first layer (`computeRlsFilter` = Layer 0 AND business RLS; `tenantLayer0FilterOf` answers an `organization_id` predicate under the `isolated` and `group` postures for every non-platform-admin caller on an object that carries the column). An organization owner there gets a filter, not `undefined`, so a producer following this contract answers `visible_to_you` and the console keeps drawing "Only records visible to you" for the owner, which is the sighting the card was filed on. Only under the `single` posture, on an object outside tenancy, or for a platform admin crossing, can the owner's answer be `all_records`. The statement stays true and fails toward the caveat, so this is not a leak; it is a contract whose stated purpose (PR body: the owner no longer gets the caveat) is not shown to be met. Required: either the description states that the organization wall counts as a row restriction and names which callers can therefore ever be `all_records`, with the PR body's claim corrected and the posture of the staging environment measured; or the route is re-put to the maintainer with this fact, since "restricted to my own organization" versus "restricted within my organization" is a product decision the two values cannot both express. The record does not choose between them.

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts`: the fail-closed rule for a producer that cannot obtain the answer lives only in the changeset ("A producer that cannot tell keeps answering `visible_to_you`"), which is release prose, not the contract a producer author reads. The `ISecurityService` contract tells hosts to OMIT a method they cannot honour and tells consumers to feature-detect, so "the answer was `undefined`" and "there was no answer" must be told apart in the schema's own words. Required: the `scope` description (and so the generated page) states that `all_records` is stated only on a `getReadFilter` call that RESOLVED to `undefined` for the same context the read ran under, and that an absent service, an absent method, a throw, or a context other than the read's own states `visible_to_you`. Detail in private.md.

Nits (no effect on correctness of the contract as written):
- `scope` is judged for `object` alone. A block with `related` lookup paths also read other objects, whose own row scope the value does not speak for. The description's "for this caller and object" is accurate; one clause saying the related paths are not covered would stop a reader over-reading `all_records`.
- "judged by the producer per call" (header) and "judged by the producer" (description) differ by "per call"; the description is what ships to the reference page, and `getReadFilter` is request-scoped and must not be memoised, so "per call" belongs in the description too.
- The console's filter row prints "All records" when no `filter` applied, beside a scope that may be `visible_to_you`. Pre-existing and outside this diff; named so the follow-up wording for `all_records` (if the console ever states it in words) does not collide with it.

`packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.test.ts`: agrees with the contract. Round-trip of `all_records`, four near-miss values and a missing key each refused on `scope` with `invalid_value`. Nothing pins the description text, which is correct for a prose change.

`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/ChatbotEnhanced.answerSource-31868.test.tsx`: agrees with the reader. The off-contract row that used `all_records` is replaced by an unknown value and a missing-scope row is added, so the "refused block draws nothing" pin is kept, not weakened.

`content/docs/references/ai/object-query-source.mdx`: truthful to the schema text; S1 and S2 apply to it through regeneration, no hand edit.

Tried and not broken: a system context (the read itself was unrestricted, so `all_records` is true); a delegated context (intersection or deny, never a bare `undefined` from a failure); a caller with no permission set (deny); a sharing-resolution outage (deny); field-level masking (not a row restriction, and the value does not claim field completeness); an older console (refuses the block whole, states nothing).

## Contract review

### ④ Design judgment

Short, because no shape moved: the delta is the contract's prose, and the judgment is whether each new sentence is true and whether S1, S2 and the nits are closed on the faces the previous record named.

`packages/spec/src/ai/object-query-source.zod.ts`, each new sentence against the code at this head.

- "The organization wall is a row restriction: under the `isolated` and `group` postures `getReadFilter` answers an `organization_id` predicate on every object that carries the column, for every caller but a platform admin whose object's posture lets them cross the wall, so an organization owner there reads `visible_to_you`." True of the code. `getReadFilter` composes `computeRlsFilter` first, which is the wall's layer AND the business row rules; under the two walled postures the wall's verdict for a tenant object is the caller's organization, the caller's organizations, or deny, and each projects to a filter, never to nothing. The one crossing is gated on true platform-admin standing together with an object posture that permits it; an organization administrator's superuser bit alone does not cross. So an org-scoped read never resolves to `undefined`, and a producer following this contract never states `all_records` for it.
- "`all_records`: stated only when that call RESOLVED to `undefined` ... for a caller no row rule or sharing narrows, that is the `single` posture, an object outside tenancy, a platform admin crossing the wall, or a system context." True, and the list is complete for the direction that matters: the only ways the wall's layer contributes nothing are the `single` posture, an object that opted out of tenancy or carries no organization column, and the platform-admin crossing; a system context returns `undefined` before any layer.
